citation: Ager, R., Styles, B., Sizmur, J., & Worth, J. (2015). Improving Numeracy and Literacy: Evaluation Report and Executive Summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (NFER evaluation of the Oxford Improving Numeracy and Literacy Programme).
report_number: EEF project: Improving Numeracy and Literacy (in Key Stage 1); ERIC ED581142
design: Efficacy RCT; school-level (cluster) randomisation; 55 schools (17 numeracy arm, 19 literacy arm, 19 shared business-as-usual control); two TPD-supported curriculum programmes (Mathematics and Reasoning; Literacy and Morphemes) delivered by class teachers after one day of training + an implementation support visit; Year 2 pupils (grade band K-2); 10-12 weeks, 1 hour/week.
problems: Two-arm report. The registry lists two row_ids (138, 139) for one report; there is no further metadata to disambiguate which arm maps to which row, so I assigned the maths/numeracy arm to the lower row_id (138 -> STEM) and the literacy arm to 139 (Reading), matching their natural ordering. Both arms share a single control group, so the same control N is used for each. EEF effect sizes are coefficient(group indicator)/pupil-level SD from a no-covariate multilevel model; the report (p.54) states this equals Cohen's d and that with ~2,000 pupils no Hedges' small-sample correction was applied (J=0.9996, negligible) -- so reported ES are effectively Hedges' g. I recomputed g and SE from the exact model coefficients/SEs (Appendix Tables A1/A2) and the standardizing pupil-level SDs; my 95% CIs reproduce the report's CIs exactly (numeracy 0.02-0.37; literacy -0.18 to 0.08). Models are pretest-adjusted and cluster-accounting (multilevel), so cluster_adjusted=true.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Mathematics and Reasoning programme (numeracy arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Progress in Maths (PiM, GL Assessment standardised maths test), age-appropriate form
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of ~12-week intervention, end of school year)
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF/NFER reported ES = numeracy-group coefficient (b=0.97, Table A1) / pupil-level SD (4.90, no-covariate multilevel model, Table A1). d=0.97/4.90=0.198; J(df=1940)=0.9996 -> g=0.198. g_se=0.44/4.90=0.0898; g_var=0.00806. Standardized by the no-covariate pupil-level SD. Reproduces report ES 0.20 and CI 0.02-0.37. n_t/n_c are analysed pupils for the maths post-test (Table 5); n_clusters = 17 numeracy + 19 control schools = 36 clusters in this contrast.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.5 (headline ES table), p.21 Table 5, p.57 Table A1
effect_sizes.notes: Primary confirmatory outcome for the numeracy arm (+3 months progress, statistically significant, 5 padlocks). Mean/SD are school-level post-test averages (Table 4, control n=19 schools, numeracy n=17 schools), shown for traceability only -- g was computed from the model coefficient and pupil-level SD, not from these school-level means.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Mathematics and Reasoning programme (numeracy arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Key Stage 1 mathematics points (national teacher-assessed attainment)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported EEF effect size taken directly from Table 5 (KS1 mathematics points, numeracy contrast). Underlying coefficient/SE not tabulated separately in the appendix, so g_var/g_se left null. 95% CI reported -0.23 to 0.16.
effect_sizes.notes: Secondary outcome: no significant impact of the numeracy intervention on KS1 maths attainment. Sample restricted to pupils with matched National Pupil Database records.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Literacy and Morphemes programme (literacy arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Progress in English (PiE, GL Assessment standardised literacy test: spelling/grammar + reading comprehension), age-appropriate form
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of ~12-week intervention, end of school year)
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF/NFER reported ES = literacy-group coefficient (b=-0.40, Table A2) / pupil-level SD (7.80, no-covariate multilevel model, Table A2). d=-0.40/7.80=-0.0513; J(df=1938)=0.9996 -> g=-0.051. g_se=0.52/7.80=0.0666; g_var=0.00444. Standardized by the no-covariate pupil-level SD. Reproduces report ES -0.05 and CI -0.18 to 0.08. n_t/n_c are analysed pupils for the literacy post-test (Table 5); n_clusters = 19 literacy + 19 control schools = 38 clusters in this contrast.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.5 (headline ES table), p.21 Table 5, p.58 Table A2
effect_sizes.notes: Primary confirmatory outcome for the literacy arm (-1 month, not statistically significant; no evidence of impact; 5 padlocks). Mean/SD are school-level post-test averages (Table 4, control n=19 schools, literacy n=19 schools), shown for traceability only -- g was computed from the model coefficient and pupil-level SD, not from these school-level means.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Literacy and Morphemes programme (literacy arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Key Stage 1 reading and writing points (national teacher-assessed attainment)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported EEF effect size taken directly from Table 5 (KS1 reading and writing points, literacy contrast). Underlying coefficient/SE not tabulated separately in the appendix, so g_var/g_se left null. 95% CI reported -0.24 to 0.13.
effect_sizes.notes: Secondary outcome: no significant impact of the literacy intervention on KS1 reading and writing attainment. Sample restricted to pupils with matched National Pupil Database records.
